summary: Milestone 2026.08.529 completed 4 experiments in 5.6 minutes, including 1 compute-bound experiment. GPU idle was observed on that compute-bound work, while the remaining experiments were synthesis-only.

slowest_experiments.experiment: Dated evidence refresh after the V529 planner marker
Checkpointed all-family exact-atom representation corpus VRAM recovery

bottlenecks_identified: GPU idle is flagged for the 2-minute checkpointed all-family exact-atom representation corpus VRAM recovery because the supplied GPU state reported 0% utilization and the timing entry is compute-bound; the available data does not identify the root cause.
Task-lifecycle telemetry is absent, so the compute-bound duration cannot be separated into launch, model-load, waiting, recovery, inference, and cleanup phases.
One idle process retained 334MB on GPU 0, leaving avoidable allocation and process-ownership ambiguity before later compute work.
improvements_suggested: Add a compute-bound GPU-engagement watchdog that samples utilization after launch and fails fast with diagnostics when the GPU remains idle.
Record task-scoped phase timing, GPU utilization, loaded-model count, and selected runner so idle intervals and scheduling decisions can be attributed to the experiment that caused them.
Add ownership-aware cleanup at experiment boundaries to release confirmed-idle GPU allocations before VRAM-recovery work.
Select DualGPURunner only when telemetry confirms that 2 or more models are loaded in parallel; the supplied data does not show such a task in this milestone.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Implement the compute-bound GPU-engagement watchdog and fail-fast diagnostic artifact.
Automate ownership-aware cleanup of confirmed-idle GPU processes and allocations between experiments.
Emit task-correlated phase, GPU, model-concurrency, and runner-selection telemetry.
meta_reflection: The 36% estimate is the upper-bound share represented by the 2-minute compute entry within the locked 5.6-minute milestone wall time, not a measured speedup. The clearest next improvement is to make GPU engagement and runner selection observable at task scope so a later retrospective can distinguish launcher failure, waiting, and cleanup overhead.
